title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Chart Plate direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Chart Plate
options.lineage: observatory chart-plate atlases: ruled coordinate grids, magnitude legends, marginal catalogue numbers
options.thesis: The analysis screen as a printed chart plate: luminous data fields ruled by coordinate grids whose numbers run out into the plate margin, and a legend that grades how much of the signal is real.
options.viewport: Deep-ink rail on the left carrying dataset plates by number; four white data plates in the centre (contour above, kinetics and spectra below, colour legend beside); chart-paper inspector on the right with the magnitude legend at its head; status bar of tabular figures along the bottom.
options.risk: Dark chrome around luminous plates reads as a lit object in a dim room; in a bright office it can drift towards an IDE theme.

raised.raise: Every object's identity is also its address — dataset ▸ version ▸ selection — printed and clickable in the status bar, so the index and the working space are the same object.
Panel headers are a word on a hairline rule: no boxes, no icons standing in for labels.
The plate margin is a data region — dense tabular figures at the edge instead of floating readouts over the data.

options.label: The Figure Page
options.lineage: journal figure pages — hairline rules, 8 pt marginalia, ranked captions beneath every panel
options.thesis: The application is the figure: every plate is a journal panel with its ranked caption, and the analysis history is the caption that grows as you work.
options.viewport: White throughout; a thin header of rules and small-caps section marks; the centre is one figure block, (a) contour over (b) kinetics over (c) spectra, each with its caption under it; a right column of caption-and-control pairs; the export row sits at the foot.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs of this category land on — a white scientific workstation with one accent is the familiar answer, and its distinctiveness depends on the captions genuinely carrying the state.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.lineage: airport sign systems: saturated yellow bands, humanist sans, monumental gate numbers
options.thesis: The screen signs itself: one message per band, the current quantity at monumental scale, and the inspector always naming the next decision.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for identification — everyone reads these instantly — and loses narrowly on clarity, because one message per band costs the density a working analysis screen needs.
options.risk: Monumental numbers on a dense working screen are a costume of the airport rather than a tool for the lab.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: boarding pass and departure board: segmented pass, tabular figures, rows that rerank in place
options.thesis: The processing chain is a segmented pass and the derived versions are a board that reranks in place, each changed row holding its alert colour until it has been seen.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — a reranking board is exactly what a recomputing version list is — and holds clarity; loses identification slightly, since a travel document is not this audience's own artefact.
options.risk: A segmented pass around every panel turns the workspace into paper ephemera rather than a screen.

options.label: Seasonal Folio
options.lineage: botanical folio plates: one subject through its stages, every plate at the same exact scale and ground
options.thesis: Every comparison renders at one shared scale on one ground, each plate captioned in ranked order so the difference between stages is the only thing that moves.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for clarity — fixed scale is a real discipline for comparing spectra over time — and holds identification through the scientific-plate tradition; loses narrowly because the folio's warmth is a plate ground, not a working screen's.
options.risk: Cream plates and engraved warmth read as a coffee-table book the moment density drops.

options.label: Event Catalog
options.lineage: convention-circle catalogues: hundreds of postage-stamp thumbnails packed into a numbered hall grid
options.case: Loses both axes: a doujin event catalogue is not this audience's ritual, and packing a working screen with hand-marked thumbnails costs the density real data needs.
options.kept: The index and the working space are one object: a selection carries its position, and the position is the link.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.lineage: metro typographic tiles: flat colour fields, giant lowercase cropped off the edge, chrome deleted
options.case: Loses both axes: its identification belongs to designers rather than spectroscopists, and a luminance-strobing tile field actively fights a screen read for subtle colour differences.
options.kept: Chrome deleted so type does the work — a header is a word on a rule, not a container.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: data-sublime fields: dense barcode columns and sine lattices in pure black and white
options.case: Loses both axes as a screen: its strobe is a mural rather than a workspace, and the identification it does hold — data graphics as a tradition — is spent on dazzle instead of on reading a value.
options.kept: The margin as a data region: dense tabular figures packed at the edge rather than floating readouts over the data.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dockable scientific workstation, executed at full craft: a dark grey shell, panels and tabs around a plot, a tree on the left, an inspector on the right.
canonCard.viewport: Grey rail, tabbed centre with a large contour plot, kinetics beside it, a version tree on the left, an inspector of labelled fields on the right, a progress strip at the foot.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the tools this audience already uses, by design.
